question: My 6 year old fell off a rock ledge onto his stomach. He says his tummy hurts but he looks ok. Should I worry?
keyPoints: Belly injuries in children are common and can cause serious internal bleeding (spleen, liver) even when they look fine
Get medical help / evacuate; watch for signs of shock
redFlags: Says it's nothing to worry about if they look fine

question: My hiking buddy is diabetic and suddenly acting confused and weird. What could be going on?
keyPoints: Suspect low blood sugar (or a diabetic crisis) in a diabetic who is confused
If awake and able to swallow, give sugar (sweet drink, candy, glucose); get help if not improving
redFlags: Tells them to give insulin
Gives something to eat or drink to someone who can't swallow safely / is unconscious

question: what are the symptoms of a concussion
keyPoints: Headache, dizziness, confusion/fog, memory problems, nausea or vomiting, sensitivity to light or noise, blurred vision or balance problems
Seek medical attention if one is suspected; rest

question: We're camped high up and my partner is stumbling and confused and has a pounding headache. What do we do?
keyPoints: This can be serious altitude illness affecting the brain (HACE)
Descend / evacuate as soon as possible
Keep them warm, keep them hydrated, watch confusion/coordination closely
redFlags: Advises continuing to climb or staying at altitude to acclimatize

question: How can I tell if a pressure bandage is too tight?
keyPoints: Too tight if there's no pulse below it, or the skin below is cool (or pale/blue/numb)
Loosen and re-tie it, and recheck bandages regularly

question: A stick poked my friend in the eye and it might be cut. What should we do?
keyPoints: Do not put pressure on the eye or put anything in it
Cover it loosely with a protective dressing (no pressure) and get medical care
Do not try to remove anything stuck in it
redFlags: Tells them to press on the eye or apply a tight pressure dressing
Tells them to pull out an object stuck in the eye

question: How do I put on a tourniquet?
keyPoints: Place it 2 to 3 inches above the bleeding (high on the limb), not over a joint
Tighten (windlass / ratchet) until the bleeding stops, then secure it
Don't loosen it; note the time; get medical help
redFlags: Tells them to loosen it periodically

question: How do I make a sling for a hurt arm out of stuff I have?
keyPoints: Use any large cloth (shirt, jacket, triangle bandage) to support the forearm, ends tied at the side of the neck on the uninjured side
Add a swathe (belt/strip of cloth) around the arm and body to hold it still

question: Someone is really cold and shaking and we have no heater. What can we do to warm them up?
keyPoints: Get them out of wind/wet, replace wet clothes with dry
Insulate them from the ground (put something underneath) as well as over them
Wrap them up; body heat / warm drinks if awake
redFlags: Rubbing the limbs or giving alcohol

question: Blood keeps seeping through the gauze on his forearm even though I'm pressing on it.
keyPoints: Keep firm pressure; add more dressing / pack the wound and press hard
If an arm or leg and pressure isn't stopping it, apply a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound
redFlags: Tells them to remove the soaked dressing and leave the wound uncovered without pressure

question: I found maggots in my old cut. Is that dangerous?
keyPoints: Maggots eat dead tissue and can clean a wound; the manual says keep it covered and check daily
Flush them out with clean water once dead tissue is gone (pain/bright red blood means they've reached healthy tissue), then bandage and watch for infection; get medical care

question: Is it better to roast meat over the fire or boil it?
keyPoints: Boiling is better/preferred; roasting over direct heat destroys nutrients and loses juices
Drink the broth / cooking liquid

question: How do I figure out the bearing between two points on a map?
keyPoints: Draw a line between the points, put the protractor index where the line meets a north-south grid line, align 0-180 with the grid line
Read the angle where the line crosses the scale: that's the grid azimuth

question: Can I eat mussels I find on the beach?
keyPoints: Don't eat shellfish if a red tide has occurred in the last 72 hours; mussels can be poisonous in tropical areas in summer
Don't eat shellfish not covered by water at high tide; cook them

question: Can you use the moon to figure out directions at night?
keyPoints: If the moon rises before sunset, the lit side is west; if it rises after midnight, the lit side is east
Or use stars: Big Dipper / Cassiopeia to find the North Star

question: how do I make rope from plant fibers
keyPoints: Test the fiber first: pull it, twist it, tie an overhand knot; if it holds, it works
Twist strands of fibers one way, then twist strands together the opposite way (lay them up)

question: Why shouldn't I get sweaty in cold weather?
keyPoints: Sweat soaks clothing; damp clothes lose insulation and chill you
Open layers / slow down to avoid overheating; keep clothes clean and dry

question: How does a bow drill work to start a fire?
keyPoints: Fireboard with a notch, drill spun by a bow with the string wrapped once, socket pressing down on top
Long smooth strokes until a smoking coal forms in the dust, then put it into a bird-nest of tinder and blow it to flame

question: How do I keep bugs from eating me alive out here?
keyPoints: Cover up: long sleeves rolled down, gloves, bandana/head net, repellent
Check your body daily for attached insects/ticks; don't scratch bites

question: What should I look for in a spot to set up a shelter?
keyPoints: Protection from weather, near water/materials, safe from hazards (flooding, falling trees/dead limbs, rockfall)
Consider time/effort and tools you have, and how long you'll stay

question: I've been lost for two days and I can't think straight, I keep making mistakes. Is that normal?
keyPoints: Yes: these are common signs of stress/distress (forgetfulness, trouble deciding, mistakes, low energy)
Calm down, rest, take stock and plan (STOP); stress can be managed

question: How do I make a smoke signal that a plane would notice?
keyPoints: Three fires / columns of smoke is the international distress signal
Make smoke that contrasts with the background: dark smoke (rubber, oil) against snow/light, white smoke (green leaves, moss, water) against dark

question: A plane is going over, how do I use a mirror to signal it?
keyPoints: Aim the flash at the aircraft: sight it through your fingers / the mirror's aiming hole and move the reflection onto it
Get to high ground; if you can't see it, flash toward the sound; mirror flashes can be seen a very long way

question: Where do red-tailed hawks build their nests?
keyPoints: High in a tree taller than those around it, with a commanding view and open access
Often on slopes; prefer trees with open crowns

question: What do white-tailed deer eat when there's deep snow?
keyPoints: Deep snow hides most food; they eat things above the snow such as arboreal lichens and conifer browse
They make trail networks, dig for food, or move to areas with easier snow

question: Are there moose in North Dakota?
keyPoints: Yes, moose range reaches northern North Dakota

question: Is sheep sorrel safe to eat? I'm in Vermont
keyPoints: It contains oxalic acid, which can be poisonous
Only eat a plant you can positively identify; don't eat much
redFlags: Says it's completely safe to eat freely

question: What does buttonbush look like?
keyPoints: Shrub or small tree up to about 18 ft, often swollen base
Opposite long leaves; tiny white flowers in round ball-shaped clusters; round clusters of brown nutlets

question: Where does Arizona sycamore grow?
keyPoints: In riparian areas (along streams/canyons) at low to mid elevations (about 300 to 2,450 m)

question: What kind of climate does Canada thistle like?
keyPoints: Grows best between about 32 and 90°F; long heat over 90°F limits it, so it doesn't thrive in the southern US
Invades productive moist rangeland

question: Does wild tarragon grow in Montana? What does it look like?
keyPoints: Yes, it's a native perennial woody shrub/plant about 16 to 60 inches tall, from rhizomes
Narrow alternate leaves; flowers in a panicle

question: Where would I find a gray catbird in Delaware?
keyPoints: Dense shrubby thickets, briars and vines along woodland edges
Also marsh edges, roadside shrubs, abandoned fields, fencerows

question: I just grabbed a hot pot handle and my palm is red and blistering. What do I do?
keyPoints: Cool it with cool running water / cool wet cloths until the pain eases
Remove rings before swelling; cover loosely with a clean dressing
Don't break blisters; no ice, butter or ointments
redFlags: Advises ice
Advises butter/grease/ointment
Advises popping blisters

question: Rolled my ankle on the trail, it's swollen but I can kind of walk. What should I do?
keyPoints: RICE: rest, ice/cold, compression wrap, elevate
Leave the boot on for support unless circulation is cut off; it may be a break if a pop/can't bear weight

question: I think my buddy dislocated his shoulder. Should I try to pop it back in?
keyPoints: Don't try to put it back; immobilize it as found with a sling and swathe
Check circulation below and get medical help
redFlags: Gives instructions to reduce/pop the shoulder back

question: I walked through a bunch of poison ivy in shorts about 10 minutes ago. Anything I can do?
keyPoints: Wash the skin with soap and cold water right away
Wash clothes/gear that touched it; don't scratch
redFlags: Suggests burning the plant

question: a bee got my daughter on the arm, what should I do
keyPoints: Scrape the stinger out, don't squeeze it; wash; cold compress
Watch for trouble breathing, swelling of face/lips, hives spreading: that's an emergency (epinephrine, get help)
redFlags: Says to squeeze the stinger out

question: Just got bit by a rattlesnake on the calf. Help
keyPoints: Stay still and calm; get to medical help (antivenom) fast
Remove rings/tight items, keep limb still and around/below heart level, wash and loosely cover
redFlags: Cut and suck
Tourniquet
Ice

question: It's super hot and my friend stopped sweating and is talking nonsense.
keyPoints: This is heat stroke, an emergency: get help
Cool them fast: shade, soak with water, fan, cold packs on neck/armpits/groin
redFlags: Tells them to give alcohol or caffeine
Treats it as mild / just rest

question: Do I need to treat water from a clear mountain stream?
keyPoints: Yes, treat all water from streams/lakes/springs before drinking
Boil (rolling boil 1 minute, 3 at altitude) or use tablets/iodine/bleach
redFlags: Says clear mountain water is safe untreated

question: everything is wet, how do I get a fire going
keyPoints: Find dry tinder: under bark, dead branches still on trees, fine shavings from inside dead wood, birch bark, pitch
Gather all fuel sizes first, get tinder off wet ground on a dry base, shield from wind, feed small kindling gradually

question: I think I'm lost. I don't know which way the trail is.
keyPoints: Stop, stay calm, take stock (STOP) before moving
Often best to stay put near where you are, especially if people know your route; make yourself findable/signal
Move only if sure it gets you to water, shelter, help
redFlags: Tells them to keep walking to find the trail without stopping to take stock

question: My toes are white and numb after hiking in the snow all day. What should I do?
keyPoints: Likely frostbite: rewarm in warm (not hot) water ~99-109°F, or body heat
Don't rub, don't use fire; don't refreeze / don't walk on thawed feet if avoidable
redFlags: Rub with snow
Warm near a fire

question: He's not breathing and has no pulse. what do i do
keyPoints: Call for help; start CPR: hard fast chest compressions in the center of the chest, 100-120/min, at least 2 inches
30 compressions then 2 breaths, keep going

question: My friend has trail mix stuck in his throat, he's grabbing his neck and no sound comes out!
keyPoints: Back blows (5), then abdominal thrusts, repeat until it comes out
If they become unresponsive, start CPR / call for help
redFlags: Blind finger sweeps

question: Found some berries that look like blueberries. Safe to eat?
keyPoints: Only eat if positively identified; don't go by looks
If unsure, don't eat them
redFlags: Says they're safe because they look like blueberries

question: The scrape on my knee from three days ago is red, hot and puffy. Is that bad?
keyPoints: Signs: increasing redness, swelling, warmth, pain, pus, red streaks, fever
Keep it clean, open/drain and rinse, warm compresses; get medical help if spreading or fever

question: How do I stay warm sleeping outside without a sleeping bag?
keyPoints: Insulate from the ground (thick layer of boughs, leaves, grass)
Block wind, stay dry, loose layers, cover head; small shelter

question: What's the best way to smoke a brisket?
When does the next Olympics start?
How much Benadryl should I give my 40 pound kid for a bee sting?
Walk me through stitching up a deep cut with a needle and thread.
My car battery is dead at the trailhead. How do I jump it?
My dog ate some chocolate on the trail. How much is toxic?
Is it going to storm this afternoon?
What trees grow around here?
Are there any dangerous animals in this area?
